newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks lose steam after burst above 10,000.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks lose steam after burst above 10,000.

text.p: Taiwan's share prices were losing steam in late trade on Tuesday as investors locked in profits after the index's dramatic burst above 10,000, brokers said.
The benchmark stock index surged as high as 10,057 but by 0315 GMT, with 45 minutes of trading to go, had slipped 8.82 points or 0.09 percent to stand at 9,914.23.
Turnover was relatively heavy at T$163 billion.
"The pressure was strong and investors were cautious" above 10,000, said Lin Long-hsien, assistant manager of United Securities.
Brokers said profit-taking pressure was strong, particularly in the electronics sector.
Electronics were down 0.74 percent, hit by an announcement by Dutch firm Philips Electronic NV that it was selling 100 million shares of chip giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.
Taiwan Semicon was down T$7 to T$149, while rival United Microelectronics, whose performance often reflects that of Taiwan Semiconductor, was down T$3 to T$136.5.
